newsitem.title: GERMANY: Boehringer Mannheim posts strong H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Boehringer Mannheim posts strong H1 profits.

text.p: Boehringer Mannheim GmbH, part of the privately owned German drugs group, was optimistic for the full year after posting a 40 percent jump in profits during the first six months of 1997.

Boehringer, which is slated to be sold to Swiss industry giant Roche AG, recorded a 15 percent rise in sales to 1.457 billion marks and a 40 percent jump in profits to around 100 million marks, the group's management board chairman Juergen Schwiezer said.
"After a very, very strong month in July, we are optimistic for the remainder of the year," Schwiezer said.
For the group as a whole, supervisory board chairman Gerald Moeller said Boehringer hoped to post a profit of around $455 million.

Boehringer Mannheim is part of the Bermuda-based Corange group. Roche in May announced plans to purchase Corange as part of a complex $11 billion deal to acquire the German diagnostics and pharmaceuticals company.
